draft.title: How form shapes meaning
card: Form is the kind of text a writer chooses, such as a novel, play, film, poetry collection or memoir. Each form has its own tools for making meaning.
meaning comes through dialogue, stage directions, set, lighting and actors' movements. It is written to be performed, so the audience sees and hears it live.
meaning comes through camera angles, editing, sound and music. A close-up, for example, can focus the viewer on a character's face and feelings.
A novel or memoir uses narration and a narrator's voice. A poetry collection uses line breaks, rhythm and imagery. In an essay, name the form's tools and explain what they suggest.
draft.remember: Each form has its own tools, so link a text's meaning to the tools its form uses.

a.q: Which choice is a feature of film rather than of a novel's narration?
opts: A slow camera zoom onto a character's face
A narrator describing a character's thoughts
A chapter that ends on an unanswered question
A character's memory told in the past tense
a.why: A camera zoom is a tool of film, because film works through images and editing. The other three are ways a written text can work, so a narrator describing thoughts is a feature of a novel, not film.

b.q: A playwright adds a stage direction that a character stands alone in dim light while others talk in bright light. What does this most likely show the audience?
opts: The character is isolated from the others
The scene takes place at the end of the day
The other characters are telling the truth
The character has just changed their mind
b.why: Lighting is a tool of the play form, and the contrast between dim and bright sets the character apart from the group, which suggests isolation. The time of day is a tempting reading, but the contrast in light between characters points to separation, not the hour.
b.clue: Look at how the light treats one character compared with the rest.

a.best: A slow camera zoom onto a character's face

b.best: The character is isolated from the others
